summary: iter104 — P0 backend regression for the 'tap a trainer from Trainee Home does NOT open profile' bug. The frontend was passing trainer-profile doc `id` to `/api/trainer-profiles/{trainerId}` which resolves by USER ID (so it 404'd). The frontend now passes `trainer.userId || trainer.id`. Backend-side contract that the fix relies on is fully verified: 9/9 iter104 tests pass + 26/26 prior iter102* regression tests still pass (3 pre-existing skips, no new failures). No backend code changes needed.

minor.issue: Response model `TrainerProfileResponse` (backend/models.py:268-332) does NOT expose `accentIntensity`, even though the underlying DB field exists (models.py:208) and PUT /accent-color writes it. The user request asked us to confirm `accentIntensity` ships on the response — it does not. Frontend currently only reads `accentColor`, so it's NOT blocking the regression, but the API surface is inconsistent. Recommend adding `accentIntensity: Optional[float] = None` to TrainerProfileResponse so the trainee-side detail screen can render accent strength.

action_items: (Non-blocking, recommended) Add `accentIntensity: Optional[float] = None` to `TrainerProfileResponse` (backend/models.py:268-332). The DB field is already written by PUT /accent-color but never surfaced back to the client.

(Verified, no action) The frontend fix in /app/frontend/app/trainee/(tabs)/home.tsx (use `trainer.userId || trainer.id`) is the correct mitigation — backend contract confirms userId is the ONLY accepted route param.

(Optional, hardening) Consider also accepting profile-doc-id as a fallback in GET /api/trainer-profiles/{id} (try {'userId': id}; if None, try {'_id': ObjectId(id)}). This would make the route defensive against the exact frontend bug that just shipped.
critical_code_review_comments: profile_routes.py:302-345 — GET /trainer-profiles/{user_id} resolves ONLY by `userId` (`db.trainer_profiles.find_one({'userId': user_id})`). There is no fallback to profile doc _id. This is correct *and* the root cause of the original P0: nearby returns BOTH `id` (doc) and `userId` and the frontend was reaching for the wrong one. Defence-in-depth fallback recommended (see action items).

location_routes.py:538-541 — /api/trainers/nearby returns `{'id': str(trainer['_id']), 'trainerId': trainer['userId'], 'userId': trainer['userId'], ...}`. Three near-synonyms in the same payload is asking for exactly this kind of bug. Recommend deprecating the bare `id` key from this response (or renaming it to `profileDocId`) so no future frontend can confuse it with the trainer's userId.
models.py:208 vs models.py:268-332 — accentIntensity is writable but not readable through the public profile response. Minor API surface gap.

session_routes.py + payment_routes.py:994-1035 — deferred-payment gate is solid: paymentReady starts falsy, accept flips it to true, payment-intent rejects 400 before agreed. iter102aq contract holds in iter104.

Pricing surfaces are consistent: tierRates, ratePerMinuteCents, outdoorRateCents all match byte-for-byte between /trainers/nearby and /trainer-profiles/{userId}. Frontend resolver has a single source of truth.

KEY INSIGHT for future testers: `/api/trainers/nearby` returns BOTH `id` (profile doc _id) and `userId` (user _id) — frontends MUST navigate to /trainer-profiles/{userId}. Passing `id` returns 404.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: location_routes.py:538-541 sets `'id': str(trainer['_id'])` (the trainer_profiles doc _id) AND `'userId': trainer['userId']` on every /nearby record. The frontend trainee home was reading `.id` for the bottom-sheet tap handler and passing it to /trainee/trainer-detail?trainerId=..., which then hit GET /api/trainer-profiles/{that_id}. The route at profile_routes.py:305 queries `db.trainer_profiles.find_one({'userId': user_id})` — so a profile doc _id never matches and the screen 404'd silently. MITIGATION (applied by main agent in frontend): use `trainer.userId || trainer.id` everywhere a trainerId is passed downstream (home.tsx lines 439-465 bottomSheetTrainers, 700-702 search tap, 830-834 favorites strip, 911-915 onSelectTrainer, 1043-1049 preview card). REPRODUCTION (backend-side, locked in this iter): `curl /api/trainer-profiles/{profileDocId}` → 404, `curl /api/trainer-profiles/{userId}` → 200. HARDENING SUGGESTION: rename nearby's `id` to `profileDocId` (or drop it) so this confusion cannot recur.
